sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:74

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:74:1
items.html: His Mochin doubled, from the side of Aba and from the side of Ima: And although AVI, too, take doubled Mochin, namely, from AA and from the Nukva of AA; and likewise AA [takes doubled Mochin] from Atik and from the Nukva of Atik. However, since AA and his Nukva are only the male and female within one body — the MA being the male in it and the BON the female in it — and likewise Atik, this is not regarded as doubled Mochin. Not so AVI: in Aba alone there is MA and BON, male and female, and likewise in Ima alone there is MA and BON, male and female; they are regarded as doubled Mochin. For in the Mochin of Aba alone there is MA and BON, a union of male and female. And likewise in Ima.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:74:2
items.html:
The Hassadim of BON joined in partnership with the Gevurot of BON in the NHY of Ima: Explanation: Aba was made from Keter, Hochma and the ZA of the Bina of MA, together with the seven lower ones of the Hochma of BON. And Ima was made from the Bina and Malchut of the Bina of MA, together with the six lower ones of the Bina of BON. And therefore there is HG in MA: the males of MA, which are Keter and Hochma and the ZA of the Bina of MA, are regarded as the Hassadim of MA; and the females of MA, which are Bina and Malchut of the Bina of MA, are regarded as the Gevurot of MA. And the seven lower ones of the Hochma of BON, which are the discernment of the male, are regarded as the Hassadim of BON; and the six lower ones of the Bina of BON, which is the Nukva, are regarded as the Gevurot of BON.
And this is what is said, “the Hassadim of BON joined in partnership with the Gevurot of BON in the NHY of Ima”: for the BON of Aba, which is the seven lower ones of the Hochma of BON, which is the Hassadim of BON, as above, joined in partnership with the six lower ones of the Bina of BON, which are the Gevurot of BON, as above; and both of them were clothed in the NHY of Ima and became Mochin in the Nukva that is in the body of ZA, which is also the discernment of BON, namely, the VAK of BON.
And this is what is said, “and the Gevurot of MA with the Hassadim of MA joined in partnership in the NHY of Aba”: for the MA of Aba, which is the Keter, Hochma and ZA of the Bina of MA, which are the Hassadim of MA, joined in partnership with the Gevurot of MA, which are the Bina and Malchut of the Bina of MA, as above; and they were clothed in the NHY of Aba and became Mochin in the male of ZA, which is also the discernment of MA, namely, the VAK of MA. And the reason for this exchange will be explained below in the adjacent item.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:74:3
items.html:
It follows that the Mochin of Ima are entirely of BON, and those of Aba entirely of MA: And we need to understand what caused this exchange. The matter is that in ZA there is MA and BON: the male in him is the VAK of MA, and the Nukva in him is the VAK of BON. And when he takes the Mochin from AVI, the Mochin of Aba must clothe in the male of ZA, namely in the VAK of MA, and the Mochin of Ima must clothe in the Nukva of ZA, who is the VAK of BON. However, in the Mochin of Aba alone there is MA and BON, and likewise in the Mochin of Ima alone there is MA and BON. How, then, will the Mochin of the BON of Aba clothe in the VAK of MA of ZA, and likewise how will the Mochin of the MA of Ima clothe in the VAK of BON of ZA, when they have no relation to one another? For MA cannot clothe in BON, nor the reverse. Therefore, of necessity, when ZA receives the Mochin of Aba and Ima, they are exchanged with him: the MA of Ima does not clothe in the Nukva of ZA, who is BON, but joins with the MA of Aba and clothes in the male of ZA, which is also the VAK of MA. And so the MA of Aba joins with the MA of Ima in the NHY of Aba and clothes in the male of ZA. And in the same manner, the BON of Aba cannot clothe in the male of ZA, which is MA, but goes and joins with the BON of Ima in the NHY of Ima and clothes in the Nukva of ZA, who is the VAK of BON. And so the BON of Aba and the BON of Ima are joined as Mochin in the Nukva that is in the body of ZA. And this is what is said, “it follows that the Mochin of Ima are entirely of BON”: for the BON of Aba joined with the BON of Ima within her NHY, and both of them became the Mochin of Ima, which clothe in the Nukva of ZA. And likewise, “the Mochin of Aba are entirely of MA”: for the MA of Ima joined with the MA of Aba within the garments of the NHY of Aba, and clothes in the male of ZA. Thus, the Mochin of Aba are all MA, and the Mochin of Ima are all BON.
And there is no difficulty from what the ARI wrote in Etz Chaim, Gate 19, Chapter 5: that Aba, the male, took half of the MA of MA, which is the right line and half of the middle line of the Bina of MA; and Ima, the Nukva, took half of the MA of MA, which is the left line and half of the middle line of the Bina of MA. See there. Thus it is explicit that Aba took Hochma, Hesed and Netzah, which is the right line, and additionally the halves of the three Sefirot Daat, Tifferet and Yesod; and Ima took Bina, Gevura and Hod of MA, which is the left line, and additionally took the half of the three Sefirot Daat, Tifferet and Yesod. But here he says that Aba took Hochma and the ZA of MA, and Ima took only the Bina and the Nukva of MA, and nothing of Daat, Tifferet and Yesod.
And the matter is that here the discourse is about the sources, that is, about the share of Aba, the male, and of the Nukva — what they took before the coupling from the ten Sefirot of the Bina of MA. Therefore he divides them according to the Sefirot: Aba, the male, took the males among them, and Ima, who is the Nukva, took the females among them. And there the discourse is about the clothing, that is, after both of them were corrected in a coupling that never ceases, face to face. Then, certainly, the ten Sefirot are divided between them according to the order of the lines within them. For in the order of the lines, the right line and the right half of the middle line are regarded as the male of the level, and the left line and its left half of the middle line are regarded as the female of the level. And this is simple.
